title: Incremental weight swap failure - SRE on-call notes and follow-up
content:
Summary:

On 2024-11-15 during a staged weight rollout of redwood/gpt-medium-v2-2024-11 to the inference fleet, ~18% of canary hosts began returning malformed token sequences (unexpected control tokens and repeated tokens), elevated decode-error rates, and a large number of safety-layer rejects. Customer-facing API error rate increased from baseline 0.02% to 0.9% for 7 minutes before the on-call initiated a rollback. Root cause: a packaging bug in the model build pipeline caused the tokenizer mapping file (token_map.json) to be omitted from the promoted artifact for one promotion target (artifact-registry:prod-us-west-2). This produced a model weights package that was incompatible with the runtime tokenizer deployed on the host image, leading to decode mismatches when the weight swap occurred in-place.

Impact:
- Duration: ~7 minutes of degraded output quality + 3–4 minute detection/mitigation window.
- Affected percentage: approx 18% of canary pool (region: us-west-2, instance group mgmt-canary-2).
- User-visible: noisy tokenization, repeated tokens, higher safety filter hits (some false positives), a spike in request latencies as downstream retried on client side.
- No PII leakage or data corruption observed. No persistent state changes.

Detection & Alerts:
- First signal: streaming decode error rate alert (stream-decode-errors > 0.5% in 1m) triggered at 2024-11-15T14:03:08Z.
- Second signal: console SLO dashboard showed increase in generated-token variance for model route /v1/generate/redwood-gpt-medium-v2.
- Pager duty page to SRE on-call (Maya) at 14:03:45Z.

Immediate response timeline (concise):
- 14:03:45Z: SRE on-call acknowledged alert.
- 14:04:10Z: Scoped to us-west-2 canary pool after correlating host tags and rollout orchestration logs.
- 14:04:45Z: Rolled the canary weight swap back by triggering rollback via rollout-api (rollout id ROLL-2024-11-15-88).
- 14:05:30Z: Recovered canary pool to previous weights; automated health checks returned to baseline.
- 14:10:00Z: Post-rollback stabilization and verification completed.

Root cause analysis (investigation notes):
- The model build CI publishes artifacts to the artifact registry for multiple promotion targets (prod-us-west-2, prod-eu-west-1). A packaging step bundles weights (weights.tar.gz) and tokenizer metadata (token_map.json, vocab.bin).
- For this release, the packaging script used a glob that unintentionally excluded files with the pattern token_map.* when running inside the CI container with an older shell (busybox ash) used by the build agent. The artifact for prod-us-west-2 was created by a build agent on that image while prod-eu-west-1 was created correctly by another agent. Promotion logic reused the same artifact name but pointed to different registry entries.
- Rollout orchestration (weight-swap controller) selects the artifact by tag (model: redwood/gpt-medium-v2-2024-11:promoted). Hosts download the artifact and perform an in-place weight swap using the on-disk tokenizer to align runtime. The runtime assumes the artifact contains a tokenizer manifest; when missing it falls back to the local container tokenizer, which in this case mismatched the weight id -> tokenizer mapping.
- Additional contributing factor: the rollout controller did not validate tokenizer checksums as part of the pre-swap checks. It only verified a weight checksum.

Evidence collected:
- Artifact registry diff: prod-us-west-2 artifact missing token_map.json (checksum mismatch).
- Host logs from mgmt-canary-2: repeated messages "decode_mismatch: token id 5024 not found in tokenizer map" and "fallback to container-tokenizer: mapping length mismatch".
- CI build logs: packaging step used `tar --exclude='token_map.*'` due to an earlier temporary exclude added for a test; change was not reverted.
- Rollout controller logs: pre-swap verification success for weights.tar.gz checksum but no check for token_map.json.

Why the canary didn't catch it earlier:
- Canary smoke tests rely primarily on inference correctness and latency but assumed tokenizer compatibility because artifacts were previously always bundled. The smoke test prompt set did not include edge-case tokens that would surface mapping gaps.
- Artifact promotion tool reuses artifact names and relies on owner discipline; there was no enforced artifact manifest validation on promotion.

Mitigation applied during incident:
- Immediate rollback of the promoted artifact reference in rollout controller to previous model tag (rollback completed at 14:05:30Z).
- Temporary enforcement: blocked promotions from CI agents running the older busybox-based image by adding a registry deny-list for artifacts created by that agent id.
- Notified build team to stop further promotions and isolate the two artifacts.

Post-incident corrective actions (short-term):
1) Package validation (1 day): Add a manifest validator step in the build pipeline that asserts presence and checksum of all required files (weights, token_map.json, vocab.bin, tokenizer-config.json). Gate promotions on manifest validation. Owner: Priya Desai, ETA: 2024-11-19.
2) Rollout pre-swap checks (2 days): Extend rollout controller to validate tokenizer checksum against artifact manifest before performing in-place swap. If mismatch, fail-fast and mark rollout as blocked. Owner: Jordan Alvarez, ETA: 2024-11-21.
3) Canary test expansion (3 days): Add synthetic prompts that exercise rare / control token sequences and token boundaries to canary smoke tests. Owner: SRE testworks, ETA: 2024-11-20.
4) Revert dangerous CI change (hotfix) and audit packaging scripts for accidental excludes. Owner: Build Infra (Samir Rao), ETA: 2024-11-16 (completed).
5) Artifact immutability policy (1 week): Stop reusing artifact names across promotion targets; require unique artifact ids with promotion metadata. Owner: Platform Eng, ETA: 2024-11-22.

Longer-term improvements (backlog):
- Integrate artifact registry with model metadata service so rollouts can verify runtime compatibility matrix (quantization, tokenizer version).
- Add automatic diff and smoke-run of artifact on promotion that executes the canonical tokenizer test suite.
- Enhance deployment traceability: record build-agent image id and packaging script hash in artifact metadata to aid future investigations.

Runbook updates (explicit edits to make):
- Under "Model rollout pre-checks": add new step to fetch artifact manifest and assert tokenizer checksum equality with local container tokenizer version.
- Add a decision flow: if tokenizer missing -> abort rollout and notify build infra + model-owner channel.
- Add smoking prompts file path and instructions for running the extended canary prompt set locally and in CI.

Open action items (owners & due dates):
- Priya Desai: implement manifest validator in CI and block promotions until validated. Due 2024-11-19.
- Jordan Alvarez: add tokenizer checksum validation to rollout controller. Due 2024-11-21.
- Samir Rao: audit and harden packaging scripts; remove any excludes that could omit essential files. Done 2024-11-16 (hotfix); follow-up audit due 2024-11-20.
- SRE testworks (unassigned): expand canary prompt set and add automated regression tests. Due 2024-11-20.
- Platform Eng: proposal for artifact immutability policy and unique ids. Draft due 2024-11-22.

Lessons learned / takeaways:
- Trust but verify: we relied on implicit contract that artifacts include tokenizers. Explicit manifests and checks are low-cost and high-value.
- Small packaging changes in CI can have outsized customer impact when rollout automation depends on artifact invariants.
- Canary tests must include edge-case tokenization checks for models where tokenizer and weights are separable artifacts.
- Auditing build agent images and their differing shell semantics is important: busybox ash vs bash globbing semantics caused a subtle file exclusion.

Appendices / useful references:
- Sample failing host log snippet: (2024-11-15T14:03:12Z) decode_mismatch: token id 5024 not found in token_map.json -> fallback -> repeated-token loop detected
- CI packaging diff (link): https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/commit/9f3b2-package-exclude-fix
- Rollout controller PR to add pre-swap checks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-controller/pull/324 (WIP)

Acknowledgements:
Thanks to build infra (Samir), rollout-controller (Jordan), model owners (Priya) and the on-call SRE rotation for fast mitigation.
